sessions.phase_label: All-grade scope and higher-grade content production

requirements.title: Curriculum-Aligned Content
requirements.definition: Topics, levels, and exercises must correspond to the applicable curriculum standards for their grade.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers standards alignment of selected content; the number of grades covered and the progression between levels are independently changeable Requirements.

requirements.title: All-Grade Toy Factory Coverage
requirements.definition: The Toy Factory mini-game content must cover all grades included in the project's intended educational range.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers breadth of grade coverage, not whether individual topics align with a grade or how levels progress within a topic.

requirements.title: Exercise Constraint Compliance
requirements.definition: Generated exercises must obey the mathematical and exclusion constraints specified for their level and activity.
requirements.boundary_note: Constraint correctness is independently testable across manually drafted, AI-generated, and pseudo-random content; it is separate from curriculum alignment and generator implementation.

requirements.title: Curriculum-Based Level Progression
requirements.definition: A topic may be divided into similar levels with bounded difficulty or number ranges to match curriculum blocks and support gradual progression.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers progression and segmentation of a topic into levels; exact question cardinality and visual representation are independently changeable.

requirements.title: One Question Specification per Level
requirements.definition: The initial content-design deliverable must provide one representative question specification for each level.
requirements.boundary_note: This concerns the number of representative questions authored during content design, not the number of runtime exercises a player may encounter.

requirements.title: Level Objectives and Descriptions
requirements.definition: Each level specification must document its educational objective and activity description.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers descriptive and objective fields in a level specification, not the exercise itself, its visual objects, or its curriculum mapping.

requirements.title: Spreadsheet Level Mapping
requirements.definition: When one question applies to multiple levels, the spreadsheet must repeat the question as a separate entry for each applicable level.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a deliverable-format and mapping rule; it is separate from how many question specifications each level requires.

requirements.title: Distinct Visual Object per Level
requirements.definition: Each level must use a different visual object in its question presentation.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers variation of the object used by each level; classification of the representation as a grid, numbered box, or base-ten blocks is separately changeable.

requirements.title: Visual Representation Type Classification
requirements.definition: Each level specification must identify its visual representation type, including supported types such as a grid of objects, a numbered box, or base-ten blocks.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the representation taxonomy and its specification, not whether the concrete object must differ between levels.

requirements.title: Reusable ChatGPT Content-Generation Prompt
requirements.definition: A well-specified ChatGPT prompt must automate topic and level content generation across grades, including positive instructions and exclusions needed for usable results.
requirements.boundary_note: The prompt is an independently requested generation artifact; it is separate from the runtime C# pseudo-random generator and from the correctness of generated exercises.

requirements.title: C# Constrained Random Exercise Generator
requirements.definition: The game must ultimately use C# pseudo-random generators to produce exercises under the defined mathematical constraints after the question designs are reviewed.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers implementation of the runtime generator; question drafting, prompt engineering, and validation of generated values remain separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Sorting Activity Problem Content
requirements.definition: The sorting activity must support appropriate sortable mathematical content, including even-and-odd numbers and arithmetic problems involving addition, subtraction, or multiplication.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers accepted problem forms for the sorting activity; range-based division into easier levels belongs to the independent level-progression Requirement.

unresolved_candidates.description: The visible exchange does not conclusively determine whether geometry, graphs, measurements, division, and fractions belong in Grade 2.
The 0–20, 20–50, and 50–100 sorting ranges are presented as an example or preference, so it is unclear whether those exact boundaries are mandatory.
Conveyor-belt setup and player interaction may represent independently requested interaction behavior, but the visible evidence is only a freelancer implementation claim without client confirmation.
The proposed value of six to eight levels per topic receives no visible client answer and cannot safely be established as a Requirement value.
All-grade coverage is established, but the exact first and last grades included in that range are not specified in the visible messages.
